title: #inc-1781: Origin overload after a cdn-edge cache key change

messages.text: [FIRING:1] TargetDown (namespace=edge cluster=prod-eu-west severity=critical)

replies.text: seeing it, checking if it's just one target or the whole path

messages.text: noticed audio starts getting weird in prod. Grafana says cache hit ratio is dropping hard on cdn-edge.

replies.text: same here, can confirm user reports are coming in on the support channel

messages.text: looking at the deploy diff now. only thing that stands out is the cache key change on audio.

replies.text: that would fit the origin spike, if we're suddenly missing on every request

messages.text: INC-1781 declared by @yu. Sev2. Investigating audio start latency and edge cache behavior.

replies.text: ack, i'll stay on edge metrics and config history

messages.text: origin fetches are up about 2x from baseline over the last 10 min. feed-builder is noisy too, but I think it's just downstream user pain.

replies.text: yeah feed-builder looks fine on its own, the slow part is after the audio click

messages.text: object storage is starting to throw throttling responses on audio fetches. that lines up with the latency jump.

replies.text: ugh, so edge miss burst is pushing all the way through

messages.text: [FIRING:1] TargetDown (namespace=edge cluster=prod-eu-west severity=critical)

replies.text: pretty sure that's a symptom, not a separate target issue. checking the actual request shape now

messages.text: can someone sanity check whether the cache key is including the full query string now? i think the change was meant to only catch a small subset of URLs.

replies.text: that's what I remember from the review, yeah. let me pull the exact edge config

messages.text: got it. hit ratio just tanked from the usual mid-90s to high-50s. that's too big for a normal variance blip.

replies.text: if it's including query params, app tracking strings would make every request unique, wouldn't they

messages.text: yep, and we do have those on most audio requests. that would explain the miss storm.

replies.text: ok that seems like the mechanism. not seeing anything wrong in feed-builder itself.

messages.text: confirming with logs and a sample of requests, most have tracking params appended by the apps or referral links. content is same, cache key isn't.

replies.text: so the change basically destroyed sharing across listeners. lovely.

messages.text: I'm seeing retries on playback start now. not a total outage, but definitely user-visible.

replies.text: agreed. let's revert the key behavior, keep the rest of the rollout alone.

messages.text: prepping rollback. validating old behavior against a few known audio URLs first so we don't step on the small set that actually need params.

replies.text: I can help sanity check the edge sample after you flip it in staging if needed

messages.text: validation looks fine. old keying is safe for the paths we care about. go ahead and roll back the audio cache key change.

replies.text: doing it now

messages.text: rollback deployed. watching origin fetch rate fall off now.

replies.text: nice, already seeing the slope change in Grafana

messages.text: [FIRING:1] TargetDown (namespace=edge cluster=prod-eu-west severity=critical)

replies.text: still noisy but should clear once the burst drains. not chasing that separately.

messages.text: hit ratio is back over 90%. audio starts are looking much better on the live panel.

replies.text: good, origin traffic is returning to the old baseline too

messages.text: support noise is dropping off. a couple of retries still, but the worst looks over.

replies.text: keeping an eye on it another few mins before we call it

messages.text: cache hit ratio stable again, object storage throttling has stopped, and latency is back in family.

replies.text: cool, i'll update the incident notes with the exact config change and the timeline

messages.text: INC-1781 resolved by @yu. Duration 44m 49s. Audio start latency returned to normal after reverting the cdn-edge cache key change.

replies.text: nice. let's make sure the action items capture the query-param normalization thing, otherwise this will bite us again
